s1.syndrome_frame: Progressively enlarging, painless, ulcerated skin lesions with blackish crusting in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: Painless nodular lesions on the forehead and right cheek
Arborizing telangiectasias and peripheral pigment on dermoscopy
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
Lesions are progressively enlarging
Lesions are painless
No fever, pain, or discharge from the lesions
Patient has a history of kidney transplant in 2004
Patient is immunocompromised
Lesions have central ulceration with hemorrhagic crusting
Dermoscopy shows arborizing telangiectasias, central ulceration with crusting, and peripheral pigment
Histopathological examination shows extensive dermal collection of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and macrophages
Intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos were identified on histopathological examination

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressively enlarging, painless, ulcerated skin lesions with blackish crusting in an immunocompromised patient

Arborizing telangiectasias and peripheral pigment on dermoscopy

shortlist.label: Cryptococcosis
shortlist.why_kept: Intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos were identified on histopathological examination, consistent with Cryptococcosis, particularly in an immunocompromised patient

shortlist.label: Blastomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: Progressively enlarging, ulcerated skin lesions with central ulceration and blackish crusting are consistent with Blastomycosis, and the patient's immunocompromised status increases the risk

shortlist.label: Histoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: The presence of intracellular organisms and the patient's immunocompromised status make Histoplasmosis a plausible diagnosis, although the clinical presentation is less typical

shortlist.label: Chromoblastomycosis
shortlist.why_kept: The lesions' appearance, with central ulceration and peripheral pigment, could be consistent with Chromoblastomycosis, although the presence of intracellular yeasts is not typical

shortlist.label: Cutaneous lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's immunocompromised status and the presence of progressively enlarging skin lesions make Cutaneous lymphoma a possible, although less likely, diagnosis

raw.rationale: The presence of intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos on histopathological examination is characteristic of Cryptococcosis, particularly in an immunocompromised patient.

rejected.label: Blastomycosis
rejected.why: While blastomycosis can cause skin lesions, the histopathological findings do not match the typical broad-based budding yeast seen in blastomycosis.

rejected.label: Histoplasmosis
rejected.why: Histoplasmosis typically presents with smaller intracellular yeasts without halos, and is more commonly associated with lung involvement.

rejected.label: Chromoblastomycosis
rejected.why: Chromoblastomycosis is characterized by the presence of sclerotic bodies on histopathology, which were not identified in this case.

rejected.label: Cutaneous lymphoma
rejected.why: The histopathological findings do not support a diagnosis of cutaneous lymphoma, as there is no evidence of atypical lymphoid cells or other characteristic features of lymphoma.
